schema: id,name,area,lat,lon,in(in|out|both),price(free|£|££),ages[min,max],kids 0-3,adults 0-3,dur hours,tags[],blurb,url,source, then either date (YYYY-MM-DD) or from/to, optional time

events.name: Diwali at the National Maritime Museum
events.blurb: Free Festival of Lights day: lantern parades, dance performances and rangoli workshops through the museum, 10.30am to 5pm. Drop in.

events.name: Blackheath Fireworks
events.blurb: The big south-east London display on the heath, with a funfair from the afternoon. Gates 5pm, fireworks 8pm. Ticketed this year, so book ahead and wrap up.

events.name: Dulwich Fireworks
events.blurb: A friendlier, earlier display aimed at families: gates 5pm, fireworks 7pm, kids' tickets for a pound.

events.name: Beckenham Fireworks
events.blurb: Croydon Road Rec. Gates 4.30pm, a low-noise display at 6pm for little ones, the main show at 7.30pm.

events.name: Bromley Fireworks
events.blurb: Bromley High School's display with a funfair. Gates 5.45pm, fireworks 7.30pm. Cheaper than the heath.

events.name: Danson Park Fireworks
events.blurb: Big display over the lake with a funfair. Gates 4pm, fireworks 8pm. Easiest by car.

events.name: Battersea Park Fireworks
events.blurb: The classic inner-London display with a fairground. Gates 6pm, fireworks 8.30pm; the Sunday show is the same. Late for small kids.

events.name: Battersea Park Fireworks (Sunday)
events.blurb: Second night of the Battersea display. Gates 6pm, fireworks 8.30pm. Quieter than Saturday.

events.name: Alexandra Palace Fireworks Festival
events.blurb: Street food, a bonfire, a drone show and the fireworks at 8pm over the whole of London. Gates 4pm. A long cold evening but a spectacular one.

events.name: Alexandra Palace Fireworks (Sunday)
events.blurb: The earlier Sunday show: gates 4pm, fireworks 6pm. The better night if you've got children.

events.name: The Clockworks open day
events.blurb: A museum of electric clocks that rarely opens at weekends. 10am to 4pm, free. One for the curious and the mechanically minded.

events.name: London Sewing Machine Museum open day
events.blurb: Monthly open afternoon, 2pm to 5pm, for a genuinely odd collection of 600 machines above a shop.

events.name: Tolworth Showtrain model railway show
events.blurb: One of the biggest model railway exhibitions in the south-east, both days of the weekend. Train-obsessed under-10s will not want to leave.

events.name: Remembrance Sunday at the Cenotaph
events.blurb: The national service and two-minute silence at 11am, then the march past. Arrive by 9.30am for a view; expect crowds and road closures.

events.name: Inside Aardman: Wallace & Gromit and Friends
events.blurb: Behind-the-scenes stop-motion sets and characters at the Young V&A, with the rest of the museum free. Closes 15 November.

events.name: Lost Worlds by Luxmuralis
events.blurb: A sound-and-light walk through the Old Royal Naval College, projecting lost civilisations onto the Painted Hall and chapel. Evening slots; book. Closes 15 November.

events.name: Schiaparelli: Fashion Becomes Art
events.blurb: The V&A's Schiaparelli survey closes this Sunday. Surrealist dresses, the lobster, the shoe hat. Book a slot.

events.name: The Last Princesses of Punjab
events.blurb: Sophia Duleep Singh, suffragette and goddaughter of Queen Victoria, told through objects at Kensington Palace. Closes this Sunday; palace entry included.

events.name: St Martin-in-the-Fields at 300
events.blurb: A free exhibition on three centuries of the church on Trafalgar Square. Twenty minutes, then the crypt café. Closes 15 November.

events.name: Winston Churchill: The Painter
events.blurb: Fifty-odd of Churchill's own paintings at the Wallace Collection, the first big show of them in decades. The permanent collection is free. Closes 29 November.

events.name: The Coming of Age
events.blurb: Wellcome Collection's free show on ageing, from adolescence to old age. Pair it with the Reading Room upstairs. Closes 29 November.

events.name: The Lord Mayor's Show
events.blurb: The City's 800-year-old parade: floats, bands, the gold State Coach, and this year a river pageant too. Procession starts late morning; stand near St Paul's or along Cheapside.

events.name: Free entry to St Paul's Cathedral
events.blurb: St Paul's drops its (steep) entry fee for Lord Mayor's Show day, 9.30am to 4.30pm. Go in before or after the parade. Galleries may be restricted.

events.name: Gun salute in Green Park
events.blurb: The King's Troop fire a 41-gun salute for the King's birthday at midday, horses and all, then a 62-gun salute at the Tower at 1pm. Loud; ten minutes of it.

events.name: Fulham Fire Station open day
events.blurb: The station's 130th birthday open day, 11am to 4pm. Engines, hoses, firefighters who let kids climb in. Free.

events.name: Wimbledon Village Stables open hour
events.blurb: Meet the horses and see the yard, 2pm to 3pm on the second Saturday of the month. Then Wimbledon Common.

events.name: Art deco and the golden age of poster design
events.blurb: A curator's talk at the London Transport Museum on the 1920s–30s poster boom. 2pm. Museum entry is separate.

events.name: Brixton Market heritage walk
events.blurb: A volunteer-led walk through the arcades and the market's history, 2.30pm to 4pm, a fiver. Eat afterwards in the Village.

events.name: Revolution 250 at The National Archives
events.blurb: Original documents from the American War of Independence, free, next to Kew Gardens. Closes 28 November.

events.name: When Barking & Dagenham won the World Cup
events.blurb: Valence House marks 60 years since 1966 with the borough's part in it. Small, free, and the manor house itself is worth a look. Closes 26 November.

events.name: Sea Shanty Festival at Cutty Sark
events.blurb: A day of shanty crews and singing workshops under the ship, 10am to 6pm, included with a Cutty Sark ticket.
